subject: a ripe, dried-out giant puffball: the fresh card's round squat shape with a dull papery olive-brown skin, a small ragged hole split open in the top and a soft puff of fine olive-brown spore dust rising from it, a light dusting of the same powder on the upper skin

Use the attached reference images, each for one purpose.
Reference image 1 shows a fresh giant puffball mushroom: draw this same object, keeping its round squat shape, size, proportions, placement in the frame and ink-and-watercolor rendering identical, changed only as follows: it has fully ripened and dried out, so the smooth white skin is now a dull, papery, olive-brown, slightly wrinkled and cracked, and a small ragged hole has split open in the top from which a soft puff of fine, dry, olive-brown spore dust rises and drifts to one side, with a light dusting of the same brown powder settled on the upper skin.
Hand-painted watercolor-and-ink game item illustration of a ripe, dried-out giant puffball with a papery olive-brown skin, a ragged hole in the top and a puff of brown spore dust, in the style of a cozy hand-illustrated survival-crafting game: visible black ink linework outlines with loose confident linework, soft watercolor and gouache shading, warm muted natural palette, gentle directional light from the upper left, slight three-quarter angle, single object only, comfortably inset from every edge with generous white margin (object fills roughly the lower two-thirds of the frame, never touching an edge), isolated on a solid flat pure white background (#FFFFFF) that fills every edge of the frame, no ground shadow, no cast shadow, no scenery, no surface, no text, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame.
